$comment: WHICH GitHub Actions jobs run locally, and for the ones that cannot, WHY NOT.
This file does NOT contain any gate's commands. Those are read from each repo's
real .github/workflows/*.yml when the gate runs, so a command added upstream is
picked up automatically and cannot silently go unmirrored. What this file adds is
the part a workflow does not state: which container image supplies the toolchain,
which Docker volume holds that repo's workspace, and the honest list of jobs the
'cannotMirror' is load-bearing. `node ci/lib/drift.mjs` fails when a workflow gains
a job that appears in neither map, which is the only thing standing between this
harness and the failure mode it exists to prevent: a local run that reports green
while certifying less than the reader believes.

workspaceChecks.why: The tool-risk detector vocabulary is one contract living as three hand-copied files in three repos. Each repo's own guard compares that repo against THAT REPO'S copy, so a class added in the agent and never copied leaves all three green while the class becomes ungovernable: the console cannot set a policy for a name the Backend tuple does not contain. Nothing inside a single repo's CI can see this; that is why it is here and not under 'mirrored'.

Mutation proof for the check above: fabricates divergent trios, including the historical interpreter-exec/fetch-then-exec/substitution-exfil incident, and asserts it goes red naming the class and the repos missing it -- plus that a missing checkout reports NOT CHECKED rather than passing. A drift check nobody has made go red has not been run.

Fifteen named sentences overstate what this programme can prove -- eight forbidden by the source material, seven by published research about this class of product -- and until this landed the only thing stopping one reaching a customer was a person remembering the list. It greps the plan's goal statement and any release note for them and fails naming the file, the line and the checklist row. It also compares the plan's prose checklist against Wave 8 Task 11's Go renderer, which is the other half of a deliberately-two-artifact design; the renderer does not exist yet and the check reports it ABSENT rather than as zero, because 0 == 0 reading as agreement is the exact defect it exists to prevent.

Mutation proof for the check above: 35 assertions over a real plan mutated on disk, including the discriminating pair that an absent renderer and a renderer encoding 15 produce different verdicts, and the case that found a real hole -- deleting ONE fence end marker merges two fences, silently exempting everything between them, and the guard passed until this case existed.

Every cross-repo check here asks one module where the other checkouts are, and a wrong answer does not raise an error -- it produces a check that compared the wrong trees, or reported a file missing that is not. 23 assertions over workspaces built on disk, including a real git worktree, cover each resolution step and the two a normal run never reaches: the upward walk, and the refusal that returns null. The discriminating case is that ci/gates.json ALONE is not a workspace -- that is true of every worktree in this programme, and mistaking one for a workspace is the defect the module was written for.

The M4.7A plan argues from evidence: over a thousand of its sentences point at a file and a line. Two failures of that are silent and both were present. A BARE BASENAME -- `main.ts:429`, `constants.ts:150-165`, `server.go:365` -- names four different files in this workspace, so the claim cannot be checked by a reader or by a script while looking like the most precise evidence there is; 744 citations were in that state. A LINE NUMBER THAT DRIFTED is worse, because it still resolves: the plan's own text said `internal/dlp/dlp.go` was 1510 lines and put `func Redact` at :1479, and on origin/main today the file is 1572 lines and Redact is at :1541. This check requires a repo qualifier on every `path:line` and resolves each one against that repo's origin/main, asserting the line exists. It cannot check that the line SAYS what the plan claims -- that is a reading, not a measurement -- and it prints what it did not look at rather than leaving a green run to imply coverage it does not have.

Mutation proof for the check above: 53 assertions over documents written on disk and resolved against the real checkouts, including both halves of the plan's named defeat test (an unqualified basename is a different failure from a line past EOF), the boundary case that citing the last line of a file is not past its end, and a missing checkout reporting NOT MEASURED rather than passing. It hard-codes no line count: the expected file length is measured from origin/main at run time, because the plan's own version of this defeat test pinned 1510 lines and the file has since grown to 1572 -- which would have made the specified defeat test pass, in the task whose whole subject is line numbers that drift.

The console's AI Security policy playground evaluates admin-typed prompts through a VERBATIM COPY of the endpoint's browser engine. Frontend's vendored-digest.test.ts compares that copy against a manifest sitting beside it -- both halves in the same repo -- so it is structurally incapable of seeing the copy and the manifest agreeing with each other while the Installers source has moved, which is exactly when the console starts demonstrating behaviour the endpoint does not have. The GitHub-side answer, vendored-upstream-drift.yml, is dispatch plus a daily cron and needs a cross-repo token; its per-PR trigger is an owner cost decision owned by Wave -1. Both checkouts are already on disk here, so this asks the question with no token, no network, and nothing a GitHub setting can switch off.

Mutation proof for the check above. Nine fabricated trios, including the blind case it exists for -- manifest and copy agreeing while upstream moved -- plus a missing checkout, a missing upstream file, unparseable JSON and an empty file map all reporting NOT CHECKED rather than a pass, and CRLF-vs-LF NOT counting as drift. If the blind case ever passes, the check has stopped doing the only job that justifies it.

Wave 8 Task 11 binds the certificate claim renderer to the plan's fenced forbidden-claims checklist and the system card's per-surface rows, and those two documents live in other repositories. Installers therefore carries a VENDORED extract of each under internal/certificate/testdata/ so that go test ./... measures the binding from a standalone checkout (ship-ledger debt item 5) -- and a vendored copy is a measurement only while it equals its source. This re-derives both extracts from the plan and the card with the Go tests' own rule and compares bytes after CRLF/LF normalisation; a missing copy or source is NOT MEASURED, never a pass.

Mutation proof for the check above: one edited byte in a copy is DRIFT naming the file and the offset, a changed source under an unchanged copy is DRIFT, a missing copy or an unterminated fence or a missing heading is NOT MEASURED, and the real plan in this checkout carries exactly the two fenced regions the fixture was cut from.

Workflow headers are operational claims. This check compares present-tense trigger claims in the first 20 header comments with the real on: keys across all seven repositories, while preserving conditional future instructions as instructions rather than misclassifying them as current claims.

Defeat proof for workflow-header-truth: a stale PUSH TO MAIN claim over a manual-plus-nightly workflow must fail with the file and line, while the conditional WHEN T-M2 LANDS instruction must remain valid.

The plan's line-level claims are meaningful only against the seven fetched origin/main revisions recorded in its generated manifest. This check refuses a stale SHA, local HEAD, branch, or behind count rather than trusting a handed-down list.

Mutation proof for the rebase manifest: seven real temporary Git repositories are generated, one Installers SHA is hand-edited, and validation must fail with the recorded and actual origin/main values.
Pins the exact no-PASS statement and all 15 sourced forbidden claims.
Defeat proof that removing one forbidden claim makes the contract guard red.
Pins the required per-class standards columns, accepted editions, and ATLAS release.
Defeat proof for a missing standards column and blank ATLAS release.

cannotMirror.build:required_checks: Polls the GitHub Checks API for this SHA to decide whether the deploy may start. There is no local equivalent of 'what did GitHub record for this commit', and faking one would defeat the gate.
cannotMirror.build:deploy: Assumes an OIDC role, pushes to ECR and rolls the ECS service. Deploys stay on GitHub deliberately: they need the cloud identity, and a deploy that can be triggered from a laptop is a deploy with no audit trail.
cannotMirror.security:rate_limit_taskdef (AWS leg): The offline self-test IS mirrored; the step that reads the live task definition needs the github-runner-backend role and is reported PARTIAL.
cannotMirror.security:rds_boundary (AWS leg): Same shape: the fixture self-test runs locally, the live security-group read does not.

cannotMirror.vendored-upstream-drift:drift: Compares the vendored engine against Installers@main over the network with a token. Cross-repo and scheduled, not a PR gate.
cannotMirror.deploy-frontend-ecs:required_checks: Reads GitHub check runs for the SHA, same as Backend's.
cannotMirror.deploy-frontend-ecs:deploy: OIDC role + ECR + ECS. Deploys stay on GitHub.
cannotMirror.render-harness:gate: Needs three processes at once -- headless Chrome over CDP, next dev --webpack, and the fixture stub -- and takes about ten minutes for 33 shots. The CI image carries no browser, and adding Chromium to ci/images/node20.Dockerfile to run it on every PR is a cost decision nobody has taken. It is also the wrong shape for a PR gate: it produces EVIDENCE about how the console looks around absent data, against a wire state the author chose, and its own README says a green run proves nothing about whether a Backend ever produces that state. It is run deliberately, per wave, and banked -- see .plans/m47a-20260822/v2-waves/artifacts/w5/. The one part of it that IS cheap and deterministic runs per-PR through Frontend's own pretest instead: check:render-harness-markers, which pins the string the harness greps for to recognise a crashed page. Without that pin, renaming a log line in app/error.tsx silently stops the harness noticing that a page crashed at all.

cannotMirror.hetzner-validate-pr:summary: Aggregates the other jobs' results through `needs:`; locally the runner's own summary is that aggregate.
cannotMirror.hetzner-deploy:*: Runs on the [self-hosted, hetzner] runner, against the production intel cluster. Not billed by GitHub and not reproducible off that box.
cannotMirror.rollback:rollback: OIDC rollback of a live service.
cannotMirror.hetzner-autobump:*: Opens and merges a PR as a GitHub App. Requires the app's installation token.
cannotMirror.hetzner-autodeploy:trigger_deploy: Fires the deploy workflow after a provenance check against GitHub's API.
cannotMirror.hetzner-autorollback:rollback: Triggered by workflow_run on a failed deploy; there is no local workflow_run.

cannotMirror.deploy-scanner-workers:deploy: OIDC role + ECR + ECS. Deploys stay on GitHub.

cannotMirror.build-and-deploy:dispatch_intel_bump: Mints a GitHub App installation token and POSTs repository_dispatch into Ceragon-Intelligence.
cannotMirror.build-and-deploy (deploy leg): This repo has no separate PR-checks workflow: audit, build, test, the task-definition policy gate and the worker-result contract all live in the same job as the deploy. Everything up to the OIDC step runs locally and the gate reports PARTIAL, which is accurate -- the deploy half genuinely did not run.

cannotMirror.fp-drift-check:check: Assumes a scoped read-only AWS role and reads production findings. Scheduled, not a PR gate.
cannotMirror.retriage-check:check: Same scoped AWS role; also opens/updates a GitHub issue.

cannotMirror.pr-checks:cli-entrypoint-tests: runs-on windows-latest. cmd/devoid's entrypoint tests exercise Windows service control, ACLs and PATH resolution; a Linux container cannot stand in. Run them on this machine with `go test ./cmd/devoid/... -count=1` from a Windows shell.
cannotMirror.finding-b-e2e:macos-matrix: runs-on macos-14. Docker cannot run macOS -- Apple's licence permits macOS VMs only on Apple hardware, and there is no macOS container runtime at all. This is the single most expensive job in the workspace (30 legs per run) and it has no local substitute.
cannotMirror.finding-b-e2e:windows-matrix: runs-on windows-2022. Windows containers need a Windows container host; Docker Desktop here runs the Linux engine. Runnable on this box directly, outside Docker.
cannotMirror.finding-b-e2e:windows-msi-uninstall: windows-2022, MSI install/uninstall against a real registry.
cannotMirror.finding-b-e2e:uninstall-sweep: matrix over ubuntu AND macos; the ubuntu legs would mirror, the macOS legs cannot, so the job is listed whole rather than half-claimed.
cannotMirror.finding-b-e2e:linux-matrix: Mirrorable in principle -- 36 legs of shell/privilege/scenario -- but each leg runs `doctor --fix` against a system systemd the container does not have. Left unmirrored rather than mirrored-but-inert. Since 2026-08-26 these legs also carry the real block/allow assertion (shim-enforcement.sh); that half IS mirrored, as finding-b-e2e:shim-enforcement, which needs no systemd. What stays unmirrored here is the per-shell PATH dimension, not the enforcement proof.
cannotMirror.finding-b-e2e:two-user-systemd: same, plus two real user accounts.
cannotMirror.release:*: Cuts and signs a real agent release. Stays on GitHub: the signing keys live there and a release built on a laptop has no provenance.
cannotMirror.internal-candidate:*: Builds and publishes a prerelease, including the Windows installer on windows-latest.
